message.content:
In Blackjack, an **Ace** is a “flexible” card: it can be counted as either **1 point** or **11 points**, depending on which value gives the hand the best chance of winning without busting.

Key points:

| Situation | How the Ace is treated |
|-----------|------------------------|
| **Single Ace + 10‑value card** | Counts as 11 → a natural “Blackjack” (21). |
| **Multiple Aces** | One Ace counts as 11, the rest as 1 (unless that would bust the hand, in which case all Aces count as 1). |
| **Ace + other cards** | The dealer/hand chooses the value (1 or 11) that keeps the total ≤ 21 and as high as possible. |
| **Splitting** | Two Aces can be split into separate hands; each new hand starts with an Ace. |
| **Doubling down** | An Ace can be part of a double‑down hand, but the Ace’s value is still chosen to avoid busting. |

So the rule is simple: **an Ace can be worth 1 or 11, whichever benefits the hand most without exceeding 21.**
